title: [Exercise] Measure the Hit Rate of Item-Based Collaborative Filtering

cues.en: So, now I'm going to give you a slightly more challenging exercise.
cues.zh: 現在，給你一個稍微更有挑戰性的練習。

cues.en: Our intuition was that for our particular data set, the user-based results looked more exciting than the item-based results, which seemed to be focused on older, more obscure film titles.
cues.zh: 我們的直覺是，對這份特定資料集，使用者式結果，比聚焦於較舊、較冷門電影的項目式結果，更令人興奮。

cues.en: But we weren't sure if they were really worse recommendations, or if they were actually better recommendations back at the time, when our test user left his ratings.
cues.zh: 但不確定，它們究竟真的比較差，還是在測試使用者當時留下評分的年代，反而是更好的推薦。

cues.en: Let's measure it.
cues.zh: 來衡量一下。

cues.en: Try modifying the EvaluateUserCF.py function to measure item-based collaborative filtering instead of user-based, and see how the hit rate compares.
cues.zh: 試著修改 EvaluateUserCF.py，改為衡量項目式協同過濾，而不是使用者式，再比較命中率。

cues.en: By looking at the SimpleItemCF.py file we used earlier, you should be able to pull this off.
cues.zh: 參考先前的 SimpleItemCF.py，應該就能完成。

cues.en: So give that a try if you're up for it, and I'll show you how I did it in the next slides.
cues.zh: 如果願意挑戰，就試試看，接下來的投影片會展示我的做法。

cues.en: It should be pretty easy to adapt our code to measure user-based collaborative filtering to item-based.
cues.zh: 把衡量使用者式協同過濾的程式碼，改成項目式，應該相當容易。

cues.en: There are just two chunks of code that need to be changed.
cues.zh: 只需要修改兩段程式碼。

cues.en: The first is telling Surprise to generate item-to-item similarities by passing False for user-based in the sim_options structure.
cues.zh: 首先，在 sim_options 結構的 user_based 傳入 False，告訴 Surprise 產生項目間相似度。

cues.en: Next, we just adapt the meat of the code from SimpleItemCF.py to work within our loop that iterates through each user, and not just a single test user.
cues.zh: 接著，調整 SimpleItemCF.py 的核心程式碼，放進逐一走訪每位使用者的迴圈，而不是只處理一位測試使用者。

cues.en: The rest of the code remains the same.
cues.zh: 其餘程式碼相同。

cues.en: When we run it, the results are a bit shocking.
cues.zh: 執行後，結果有點震撼。

cues.en: Our hit rate from item-based collaborative filtering is only 0.5%, compared to 5.5% for user-based.
cues.zh: 項目式協同過濾的命中率只有 0.5%，使用者式卻有 5.5%。

cues.en: Why is this?
cues.zh: 為什麼？

cues.en: We've convinced ourselves that item-based should be a superior approach, and that's been proven in industry.
cues.zh: 我們已經說服自己，項目式應該更好，業界也驗證過。

cues.en: It's hard to prove, but I think it's just a quirk of the data set that we're using.
cues.zh: 很難證明，但我認為這只是所用資料集的特殊情況。

cues.en: The MovieLens data set was initially created about 20 years ago, and it has more data from back then than it does for current movies.
cues.zh: MovieLens 資料集最初是在大約二十年前建立，因此那個年代的資料，比當代電影更多。

cues.en: We've seen that item-based seems to focus on these older movies as a result, and this is probably leading to bad hit rates when we're looking at more modern users in the data set.
cues.zh: 我們看過，項目式因此似乎比較聚焦於舊電影；查看資料集中的較現代使用者時，這可能導致較差的命中率。

cues.en: It's just a hypothesis, but the moral of the story again is that it's hard to really evaluate recommender systems offline, especially when you're using historical, smaller data sets to test with.
cues.zh: 這只是個假設，但再次提醒，離線評估推薦系統很難，尤其使用歷史性的較小資料集測試時。

cues.en: If we were to decide on an approach based on the results of this last exercise, we would conclude that user-based collaborative filtering is far superior and reject the item-based approach.
cues.zh: 如果根據最後這個練習的結果選方法，就會認為使用者式協同過濾遠優於項目式，因而捨棄項目式。

cues.en: But if we were to test both algorithms on real-world people using real-world data in an A/B test, the results could end up being very different.
cues.zh: 但如果在真實世界，用真實資料，對真實使用者做 A/B 測試，結果可能非常不同。
